stages.title: Discover
stages.goal: Choose a business idea that fits your skills, audience, and available resources.
stages.deliverable: A validated website-business concept and problem statement.
stages.summary: Start with what you know, who you can help, and what problem is worth solving.
tasks: List your skills, interests, resources, and constraints.
Choose one audience you understand or can reach.
Write the problem your website or business will solve.
Validate the idea with three quick evidence checks.

worksheet.label: What skills, experience, or resources can you use?
Who do you want to help first?
What painful or useful problem will the website solve?
What evidence shows people may want this?

stages.title: Plan
stages.goal: Turn the idea into a simple website brief, sitemap, and business model.
stages.deliverable: A project brief with target customer, offer, pages, and sitemap.
stages.summary: Decide what the website must say, what it must do, and how it supports the business.
tasks: Draft a sitemap and project brief.

stages.title: Build
stages.goal: Choose a build method and assemble the essential website pages.
stages.deliverable: A working draft website with brand, content, and core pages.
stages.summary: Pick the right path: no-code, CMS, custom development, or assisted KSL build.

worksheet.label: Which build method fits your budget and skill level?

stages.title: Launch
stages.goal: Publish the website and confirm it works on real devices.
stages.deliverable: A public website with domain, analytics, tested links, and working forms.
stages.summary: Make the project real: deploy, connect, test, and document what changed.
tasks: Test performance, forms, links, and responsiveness.

worksheet.label: Paste launch notes, test results, or blockers.

stages.title: Rank
stages.goal: Make the website understandable to search engines and useful for searchers.
stages.deliverable: Optimized titles, descriptions, headings, internal links, sitemap, and submission checklist.
stages.summary: SEO is not magic. It is clarity, structure, evidence, and useful pages.

worksheet.label: What searches should your pages answer?

stages.title: Market
stages.goal: Create a practical content system that brings attention back to the website.
stages.deliverable: A channel choice, content pillars, and a simple publishing calendar.
stages.summary: Turn your website pages and building journey into useful public proof.

worksheet.label: What three topics can you post about repeatedly?

stages.title: Monetize
stages.goal: Choose one clear income model and conversion path.
stages.deliverable: An offer, price, buying path, and first conversion experiment.
stages.summary: Make the website ask for a sensible next step, not just admiration.

worksheet.label: What exactly can someone buy, book, or request?

stages.title: Operate
stages.goal: Set up simple workflows for inquiries, customers, delivery, and finances.
stages.deliverable: A basic operating system for leads, tasks, income, expenses, and support.
stages.summary: A small business gets calmer when repeated work has a home.

worksheet.label: What happens after someone contacts or buys from you?

stages.title: Scale
stages.goal: Use real numbers to decide what to improve next.
stages.deliverable: A 30-day and 90-day growth plan with measurable targets.
stages.summary: Growth becomes practical when bottlenecks, process, and targets are visible.
tasks: Review traffic, leads, conversion, and revenue.
Automate or document one repeated task.

worksheet.label: What will you improve in the next 30 and 90 days?
